conjecture: EJ = KP_y
reason:

(1) Since FG is a diameter, j (through F, parallel to the tangent f at G) is the tangent at F. So V = g ∩ j is the intersection of the tangents at E and F, which gives VE = VF.

(2) Because j ∥ f, the angle between chord GE and j at D equals the angle between GE and f at G. That is the tangent–chord angle ∠CGE, and it equals ∠CEG, the angle between GE and g at E. So triangle VDE is isosceles with VD = VE.

(3) HJ ∥ DE, so triangle VHJ is similar to triangle VDE and VH = VJ. Subtracting (2) gives DH = |VH − VD| = |VJ − VE| = EJ.

(4) K lies on e, which is perpendicular to j at D. KP_y ∥ j, and P_yH ∥ h1 ∥ e ⊥ j. So K, P_y, H, D form a rectangle and KP_y = DH.

Hence EJ = DH = KP_y for every P_x. Numerically, EJ² ≈ 128.71 ≈ KP_y².

Next, triangle VDE is isosceles with VD = VE. By the tangent-chord angle, angle VED = angle EFG = 90° − angle EGF, because angle GEF = 90°. Also angle VDE = 90° − angle DGF, because j ⊥ GF. Line e is perpendicular to j at D, so e is parallel to GF, and h1 is perpendicular to j at V. Put F at the origin with j as the x-axis, V = (v,0), D = (2v,0) and P_x = (v,t). Then K = (2v, 2t). Since f is parallel to j, that angle also equals the angle at D between GE and j. So triangle VDE is isosceles with VD = VE. Next, e is perpendicular to j at D, and H is the foot on j of the line from P_y parallel to h1 (and h1 is parallel to e). So line e and line P_yH are both perpendicular to j. KP_y is parallel to j, so it is the gap between these two parallel lines, measured along j: KP_y = DH. This holds for every P_x. Combining the two results gives EJ = DH = KP_y. (3) KP_y is parallel to j, and both e and the line P_yH are perpendicular to j. So KP_y projects onto j as the segment DH, giving KP_y = DH = |VH − VD|. (4) HJ ∥ DE with H on line VD and J on line VE. By similar triangles VH/VD = VJ/VE, and since VD = VE this gives VH = VJ.
